my_own_diagnosis: From xbase alone, the symptom is laptop-specific Bluetooth crackling that works fine with the phone and started recently — this is consistent with several explanations (driver/profile issues, RF interference, headphone battery) without a clear winner. Adding the focal_diagnostic_feature (crackling stops strictly at one meter from the laptop), a competent practitioner would immediately identify laptop-local RF emission as the cause, ruling out any distance-invariant explanation such as profile misconfiguration.
focal_notes: The strict proximity-dependence to the laptop is a strong, unambiguous diagnostic marker for laptop-local RF emission that a competent practitioner would correctly interpret and use to rule out the profile-misconfiguration distractor.

direction_overlaps.why: Both predict location-dependent crackling at the user's desk; however, the focal feature specifies the symptom clears at ~1 m from the laptop in any direction, which is more consistent with a laptop-centred radiation source than room-geometry reflections — the mechanisms and remediation differ enough to keep them distinct, but a judge without the exact distance framing could conflate them.

oracle_notes: HL/LL cells correctly receive the low-diagnostic oracle (ask clarifying questions, do not adopt the profile story) and HH/LH cells correctly receive the focal oracle (investigate RF interference from laptop hardware); the cell mapping is fully consistent.
